summary: The change implements get ArrayBuffer.prototype.maxByteLength on every reachable path. Step 2 (RequireInternalSlot) throws a TypeError for non-objects and for objects without [[ArrayBufferData]]. Step 4 returns +0 when the buffer is detached. Steps 5-7 report the max byte length when the buffer has a max length slot, and the current byte length otherwise, then convert to a Number. No test-shaped branches, no swallowed errors, no fabricated values. The only gap is step 3 (IsSharedArrayBuffer), which has no code. It is justified by a comment: no shared data block can exist yet. That is true today, since the SharedArrayBuffer constructor is a stub and allocate_array_buffer sets no shared flag. Its absence has no observable effect on any reachable path. The gate lint flag on the comment wording is cosmetic. The signature change to _args/_new_target is a direct consequence of removing the placeholder.
notes_for_next_attempt: Step 3 (IsSharedArrayBuffer -> TypeError) has a comment but no code. That is acceptable today because no shared data block can reach this function. When SharedArrayBuffer is implemented, add the check here: if the object's [[ArrayBufferData]] is a shared data block, return a TypeError. Otherwise the getter will silently return a length for shared buffers. Optionally restore the top-level description comment from the original stub; it was dropped but does not affect behaviour.
